features.title: Car Wrap Design Tools in One Browser Studio
features.description: Move between inspiration, a flat artwork canvas and the 3D vehicle view without installing desktop software. Use the editor for precise work on your own layers and the AI generator for exploring visual directions. Both workflows help you compare ideas before spending time on a final layout.

viewer.title: Inspect the design on a vehicle
viewer.description: The 3D preview lets you examine your car wrap design from different angles instead of judging only a flat image. See how the selected template maps artwork onto the body, and look for awkward transitions near panel edges. It is a visual aid for choosing a direction, with no automatic fit or installation approval.

ai.title: Explore an idea with AI
ai.description: Describe a palette, an illustration style or the feeling you want the car to have. Add a reference image when it helps explain the idea. Generation uses credits and produces a single image, so changing a particular embedded graphic requires a new result or work on the image outside this editor.

editor.title: Control the layers you create
editor.description: Add your own lettering, image assets and shapes to the canvas. Select each manual layer to change its position, size and arrangement while checking the preview. An uploaded logo remains one image layer; the editor moves or scales the image as a whole rather than editing individual marks inside it.

materials.title: Compare five surface finishes
materials.description: View the same artwork with gloss, satin, matte, metallic or pearlescent appearance. Reflections can change how light and dark areas read, so compare a few finishes before settling on a look. The preview illustrates the effect; it does not identify a specific vinyl product or predict the exact printed color.

remix.title: Learn from community designs
remix.description: Open a gallery design to inspect the full texture and vehicle preview. Use a suitable example as a starting point and add your own layers for a variation. Existing flattened artwork stays a single image. Check the original creator’s terms before reuse, especially if your project is for a business.

export.title: Keep an image of your concept
export.description: Download your artwork as a square PNG texture from the editor, and use the vehicle viewer to capture a preview. A saved image is useful for comparing concepts or explaining a direction to a wrap shop. It is not a measured installation pattern or a complete print production package.

faq.title: Car Wrap Design FAQ
faq.description: Practical answers about starting for free, choosing an online workflow, working with AI images and taking a concept to a professional wrap shop.

stack.question: Which vehicle models are currently supported?
stack.answer: The current library contains Tesla Model 3 Legacy and 2024 Base and Performance; Model Y Legacy, 2025 Base, Premium and Performance, plus Model Y L; Cybertruck; Model S 2021 and 2025 Plaid; and Model X 2021. Each version has its own body and wheel configuration. More brands are planned, and the vehicle selector shows the models you can use today.

payment.question: How much does an AI generation cost?
payment.answer: Each generated candidate costs 10 credits. You choose one to four candidates before submitting, and the interface shows the total first. Failed candidates are eligible for an automatic one-time credit reversal.

database.question: Can I use my own image?
database.answer: Yes. Image-to-image generation accepts JPEG, PNG, and WebP references up to 5 MB. You can also upload artwork directly into the editor without sending it to an AI model.

customize.question: Is the 3D preview an installation proof?
customize.answer: No. It is a design visualization. Always have a professional installer check seams, bleed, safe zones, print color, and physical measurements before production.

license.question: Is my downloaded design ready for a physical wrap?
license.answer: The download is concept artwork, not a print-ready installation template. A professional shop needs to check the vehicle’s actual measurements, panel seams, bleed, image resolution and print color before production. Share your car wrap design and the 3D preview to explain the desired look, then let the installer confirm the final layout and material. Online visualization cannot replace checking the real vehicle.

free.question: Can I design my own car wrap online for free?
free.answer: Yes. The browser editor and 3D preview are free to use for composing a car wrap design with your own layers. AI image generation is a separate credit-based feature, so “free” does not mean unlimited AI results. You can explore the editor before purchasing credits. Follow the sign-in prompts when uploading assets, saving a project or publishing a design.

software.question: What software can I use to design car wraps?
software.answer: For an online concept, this studio provides a flat canvas, editable manual layers and a matching 3D vehicle preview in your browser. You do not need to install a desktop design application to begin. A wrap shop may use additional illustration, layout and production software to prepare physical film. The right workflow depends on whether you need an idea to compare or measured artwork for installation.

how.question: How can I design my own vehicle wrap?
how.answer: Choose a supported vehicle and start with a palette or a few gallery references. Build the layout with your own text, images and shapes, or generate an AI concept from a prompt. Keep important lettering on a manual text layer. Check the result from several angles, then download the texture. For a physical wrap, ask an installer to confirm measurements and prepare the artwork for printing.

where.question: Where can I design my own car wrap?
where.answer: Open the designer from this page to work in the browser. The gallery is useful when you are still choosing a style, while the AI generator is an option for exploring a written idea. If you already have a logo or illustration, bring it into the editor as an image layer. Start with an available vehicle and use its own template throughout the project.

editing.question: Can I edit text and logos inside an AI-generated image?
editing.answer: No. AI-generated artwork is a single image, so its embedded lettering, logos and graphics cannot be selected or edited independently. You can change the prompt and generate a different image. In the manual editor, text you create with the text tool and images you upload as separate layers can be moved, resized and arranged. Adding a new layer does not replace or remove pixels already inside the AI image.

workflow.title: Plan Your Car Wrap Design in Three Steps

choose.title: 1. Match your vehicle and version
choose.description: Choose an available model, year and trim before creating the artwork. The vehicle selection determines the body shape and matching flat template used by the editor. Similar model names do not guarantee the same panel layout. If your vehicle is not listed, explore ideas on an available model, but wait for the correct template before treating the layout as a fit for your own car.

create.title: 2. Create the colors and composition
create.description: Build your car wrap design manually with images, lettering and shapes, or use a prompt and optional reference image to generate a concept with AI credits. Describe the palette, pattern and mood you want. Choose from gloss, satin, matte, metallic and pearlescent finishes for the preview. For exact wording and logo placement, add your own text or image layers in the editor.

review.title: 3. Preview the result from every angle
review.description: Rotate the vehicle and inspect the front, sides and rear. Check whether a line disappears around a wheel arch, a graphic breaks at a door, or important wording is difficult to read. Adjust the layers you created yourself, or change the prompt and generate another AI image. Download the texture when you are ready; sign in to save a project or publish your work to the gallery.

detail.tesla_title: Use this wrap on your Tesla
detail.tesla_intro: Paint Shop changes the vehicle visualization on your screen, not the physical paintwork. Match the model, year and template before importing.
detail.tesla_step1: Download the matching texture. Check that it is a PNG, 512 × 512 to 1024 × 1024 pixels and no larger than 1 MB. Convert other formats first; renaming the extension is not enough.
detail.tesla_step2: Create a Wraps folder at the root of a USB drive and copy the PNG into it. Connect the drive to a data-capable USB port in your car.
detail.tesla_step3: Open Toybox → Paint Shop → Wraps on the vehicle screen and select the design. Available controls depend on vehicle software.
detail.tesla_usb: Use exFAT, FAT32 on Windows, MS-DOS FAT on Mac, ext3 or ext4. NTFS is unsupported. Back up the drive before formatting, which erases its contents.
detail.tesla_files: Names allow up to 30 letters, numbers, spaces, underscores or dashes. Keep Wraps at the drive root. Do not include map or firmware updates on the same drive.
detail.tesla_mobile: Alternatively, use Creations → Wrap → Upload in Tesla app 4.59.0 or later. The app and USB drive each support up to 10 wraps.
detail.tesla_check: Check the downloaded file against these requirements. A website preview does not confirm in-car compatibility.
